method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement' (ratified 25 November 2016). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © The Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (no licence or reproduction permission in the PDF or on the site) (read at the PDF itself and the csanz.edu.au site footer). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **HCM is left ventricular hypertrophy arising from the heart muscle itself,** not explained by aortic stenosis, hypertension, thyroid disease or other loading. It may affect as many as 1 in 200 people, making it the most common inherited heart condition.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Inheritance is autosomal dominant with variable penetrance:** each child of an affected parent has a 50% chance of carrying the mutation, regardless of sex.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Under age 35, HCM is the leading structural cause of sudden cardiac death,** competitive athletes included. Death happens most often during or just after exertion, though it can occur at rest.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Symptoms range from none to heart failure and sudden death,** and include angina-type chest pain, breathlessness (including orthopnoea and nocturnal dyspnoea), fatigue, syncope or near-syncope, and palpitations.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **On examination:** a jerky, rapidly rising pulse, a prominent LV impulse, and an apical systolic murmur that gets louder with Valsalva (dynamic obstruction); a fourth heart sound is common. The ECG may show LVH voltage, T-wave inversion and Q waves.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Echocardiography is the key test:** in adults a maximal LV wall thickness of 15 mm or more is diagnostic, while 13–14 mm counts as borderline except in a family with definite HCM. It also shows cavity size, systolic and diastolic function, outflow tract obstruction and mitral regurgitation.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider phenocopies, especially when hypertrophy is concentric rather than asymmetric:** infiltrative disease such as Fabry disease and amyloidosis, and glycogen or lysosomal storage disorders.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cardiac MRI uses the same 15 mm threshold** and adds quantification of fibrosis by late gadolinium enhancement and better views of regions echo misses, such as apical HCM.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Exercise testing and Holter monitoring, plus the family's cardiac history,** help confirm the diagnosis and build a sudden-death risk profile.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Major risk factors:** previous cardiac arrest or ventricular tachycardia; family history of premature sudden cardiac death; LV wall thickness of 30 mm or more; documented non-sustained VT (3 or more beats at 120 bpm or faster); and unexplained syncope.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most clinicians advise an ICD if a patient has even one of the five major factors,** although some argue for requiring at least 2.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other factors add risk:** abnormal blood pressure response to exercise, myocardial ischaemia, LVOT obstruction of 30 mmHg or more (at rest or provoked), late gadolinium enhancement, presentation before age 21, and a large left atrium. Early data suggest LGE above 15% of LV myocardium matters.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **When only minor factors are present, the ICD decision is hard;** weigh clinical judgement with what the patient wants.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The HCM Risk-SCD score estimates 5-year sudden-death risk** from these factors plus LVOT gradient, left atrial size and age: under 4% low, 4–6% intermediate, over 6% high. At the time it was still being validated in other cohorts.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **At least 13 genes cause HCM, mostly sarcomeric** (notably MYH7 and MYBPC3). One mutation is enough; people carrying two or three mutations may have more severe disease.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Testing the 10 commonest genes finds a cause in 40–50%, rising to 70–80% with a definite family history.**
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Finding the family mutation allows cascade testing:** relatives who test negative can be spared lifelong surveillance, and the result can inform preimplantation and antenatal testing.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Genetic counselling must come before any genetic test,** and testing is best done in a specialised multidisciplinary clinic.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Options run from no treatment and lifestyle change (every patient should avoid competitive sport),** through drugs (beta-blockers, diuretics or calcium channel blockers), to surgical septal myectomy or alcohol septal ablation for significant outflow obstruction that stays symptomatic despite drugs.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **An ICD is the most effective protection against sudden death for those at highest risk,** clearly better than the older empirical use of amiodarone or beta-blockers.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Screen every first-degree relative:** at minimum a cardiologist's examination, an ECG and a transthoracic echo; cardiac MRI is increasingly used too.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suggested screening intervals, tailored to each person:** ages 12–20 every 1–1.5 years; 21–40 every 2–3 years; over 40 every 3–5 years. Under 12 (0–11) it is optional unless there is suspicion, symptoms or a malignant family history.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Surveillance is lifelong but less frequent with age;** screening second-degree relatives is decided family by family.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take a detailed family history,** including the age and circumstances of any death, and retrieve medical records and post-mortem reports; sudden cardiac death in a relative counts as a major risk factor.
claims.locator: Cardiac Society of Australia and New Zealand (CSANZ), Cardiovascular Genetic Diseases Council, 'Diagnosis and Management of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy – Position Statement', ratified 25 November 2016, https://www.csanz.edu.au/Common/Uploaded%20files/Smart%20Suite/Smart%20Library/08e39ca0-febb-4d7e-adfa-0b9af2a70795/Diagnosis%20and%20Mangement%20-%20Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy%20(2016).pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23
